variants.question: The Equator divides the Earth into which two hemispheres?
variants.explanation: Latitude 0 splits north from south.

variants.question: About how long is the Earth's circumference at the Equator?
variants.explanation: The equatorial circumference is about 40,075 km.

variants.question: Which small country lies in the Pyrenees between France and Spain?
variants.explanation: It is a co-principality in the eastern Pyrenees.

variants.question: Which river forms much of the border between Germany and Poland?
variants.explanation: The Oder and its tributary the Neisse mark the border.

variants.question: Paris is the capital of France. On which river does it stand?
variants.explanation: Paris lies on the Seine.

variants.question: Which district of Paris is home to the Eiffel Tower, in the arrondissement numbered 7?
variants.explanation: The Eiffel Tower stands on the Champ de Mars in the 7th arrondissement.

variants.question: Which lake bordering Chad, Cameroon, Niger and Nigeria has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s?
variants.explanation: Drought and water use have shrunk it greatly.

variants.question: Which dry, dusty wind blows from the Sahara across West Africa in winter?
variants.explanation: The Harmattan carries fine dust that reduces visibility.

variants.question: From which direction do the summer monsoon winds mainly reach India?
variants.explanation: Moist air flows in from the Indian Ocean.

variants.question: Cherrapunji and Mawsynram, among the wettest places on Earth, are in which Indian state?
variants.explanation: They lie on the Khasi Hills, which catch monsoon air.

variants.question: The Köppen system classifies world climates mainly by what?
variants.explanation: It uses temperature, precipitation and vegetation.

variants.question: Which climate has hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters, as around the Mediterranean and in California?
variants.explanation: It also occurs in central Chile and parts of Australia and South Africa.

variants.question: What does the Mercator projection exaggerate most?
choices: The size of areas far from the equator
The size of areas near the equator
variants.explanation: Scale grows with latitude, so Greenland and Russia look much bigger than they are.

variants.question: Which property does the Mercator projection preserve, which made it useful for sailors?
choices: Angles, so a constant compass bearing is a straight line
variants.explanation: Mercator is conformal: it keeps local angles but distorts area.

variants.question: From which country did the United States buy Alaska in 1867?
variants.explanation: The US bought Alaska from the Russian Empire.

variants.question: Alaska became the 49th US state in which year?
variants.explanation: Alaska achieved statehood in January 1959.

variants.question: The Strait of Malacca separates the island of Sumatra from which peninsula?
variants.explanation: It is a major shipping lane between the Indian and Pacific oceans.

variants.question: Which Indonesian island is the most populous island in the world?
variants.explanation: More than 140 million people live on Java.

variants.question: Perth is the capital of which Australian state?
variants.explanation: It is Australia's largest state by area.

variants.question: Which strait separates Tasmania from mainland Australia?
variants.explanation: Bass Strait links the Indian and Pacific oceans' waters.

variants.question: Zurich is Switzerland's largest city. Which city is the seat of its federal government?
variants.explanation: Bern is the federal city; Switzerland formally has no legally designated capital, but Bern hosts the government.

variants.question: Which of these countries has more than one capital city?
variants.explanation: South Africa has three: Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative) and Bloemfontein (judicial).

variants.question: Which of these is doubly landlocked, meaning all its neighbours are landlocked too?
variants.explanation: Liechtenstein borders only Switzerland and Austria, both landlocked. Switzerland borders France and Italy, which have coasts.

variants.question: Which of these countries is doubly landlocked?
variants.explanation: Uzbekistan and Liechtenstein are the only two. Kazakhstan and Mongolia border Russia and China, which have ocean coasts.

variants.question: The Sahara covers much of which continent?
variants.explanation: The Sahara stretches across northern Africa.

variants.question: Which is the largest desert in the world overall, counting cold deserts?
variants.explanation: Antarctica is the largest desert by area.

variants.question: Which is the smallest of the Great Lakes by area?
variants.explanation: Ontario covers about 19,000 square kilometres, less than any of the other four.

variants.question: Which Great Lake is the shallowest, averaging only about 19 metres deep?
variants.explanation: Lake Erie is the shallowest of the Great Lakes.

variants.question: Victoria Falls lie on the border of which two countries?
variants.explanation: The Zambezi forms the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe at the falls.

variants.question: About how wide is Victoria Falls?
variants.explanation: Victoria Falls spans about 1,700 metres, one of the widest curtains of falling water in the world.

variants.question: Which river carries the water over Niagara Falls?
variants.explanation: The Niagara River flows from Lake Erie to Lake Ontario over the falls.

variants.question: About how high is the drop of the Horseshoe Falls at Niagara?
variants.explanation: The Horseshoe Falls drops roughly 50 metres.

variants.question: Mont Blanc stands on the border of France and which other country?
variants.explanation: It lies in the Graian Alps.

variants.question: The Alps rose mainly from the collision of the Eurasian plate with which plate?
variants.explanation: Africa and Adria pushed northwards into Europe.

variants.question: In which ocean is the Mariana Trench, the deepest known part of the seabed?
variants.explanation: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench lies in the western Pacific.

variants.question: About how deep is the Challenger Deep, the deepest known point of the oceans?
variants.explanation: The Challenger Deep is roughly 10,900 to 11,000 metres below sea level.

variants.question: Which line of latitude lies at about 66.5° north?
variants.explanation: North of it, the Sun can stay above or below the horizon for 24 hours.

variants.question: Which line of longitude passes through Greenwich, in London?
variants.explanation: It is defined as 0° longitude.

variants.question: Which 1959 treaty reserves Antarctica for peaceful and scientific use?
variants.explanation: It entered into force in 1961.

variants.question: Which Antarctic sea contains the Ross Ice Shelf?
variants.explanation: The shelf is named after the British explorer James Clark Ross.

variants.question: Which salt lake, bordering Israel and Jordan, is the lowest point on land?
variants.explanation: Its shore lies more than 430 metres below sea level.

variants.question: Which strait connects the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman?
variants.explanation: It is a narrow, strategically important passage for oil tankers.

variants.question: The Seine flows into which body of water?
variants.explanation: It enters the Channel near Le Havre.

variants.question: Which cathedral stands on the Ile de la Cite, an island in the Seine?
variants.explanation: Notre-Dame is on the Ile de la Cite.

variants.question: Which two Niles meet at Khartoum to form the main Nile?
choices: The Blue Nile and the White Nile
variants.explanation: They join in Sudan's capital.

variants.question: In which country does the Blue Nile rise, from Lake Tana?
variants.explanation: Lake Tana lies in the Ethiopian highlands.

variants.question: Into which sea does the Danube empty?
variants.explanation: Its delta lies in Romania and Ukraine.

variants.question: Which is the longest river entirely within Europe?
variants.explanation: The Volga is about 3,500 km long.

variants.question: Through or along how many countries does the Mekong flow?
variants.explanation: The Mekong flows through or along China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam.

variants.question: In which country does the Mekong form its huge delta, a major rice-growing region?
variants.explanation: The Mekong Delta is in southern Vietnam.

variants.question: Just before reaching Egypt, the Nile flows through which country?
variants.explanation: The Nile crosses Sudan before entering Egypt at Lake Nasser.

variants.question: The Nile basin is shared by how many countries?
variants.explanation: Eleven countries share the Nile basin, from Burundi and Rwanda to Egypt.

variants.question: The Yangtze flows into which sea at Shanghai?
variants.explanation: At Shanghai the Yangtze empties into the East China Sea.

variants.question: About how long is the Yangtze?
variants.explanation: Estimates put the Yangtze at roughly 6,300 km. Only the Nile and the Amazon are longer.

variants.question: How many times does the Congo River cross the Equator?
variants.explanation: The Congo crosses the Equator twice because of its great arc through the basin.

variants.question: The Congo is the deepest river known. In places it is deeper than about how many metres?
variants.explanation: In places the Congo is more than 220 metres deep, deeper than any other river known.

variants.question: About how long is the Volga?
variants.explanation: The Volga is about 3,530 km long.

variants.question: Which city lies on the Volga delta, close to the Caspian shore?
variants.explanation: Astrakhan stands in the Volga delta, a few dozen kilometres from the Caspian Sea.

variants.question: Into which gulf does the Niger empty through a huge delta?
variants.explanation: The Niger Delta in Nigeria opens onto the Gulf of Guinea.

variants.question: About how long is the Niger?
variants.explanation: The Niger runs for roughly 4,200 km in a great boomerang-shaped arc.

variants.question: The Murray forms most of the border between which two Australian states?
variants.explanation: The Murray marks most of the boundary between New South Wales and Victoria.

variants.question: About how long is the Murray?
variants.explanation: The Murray is about 2,500 km long.

variants.question: Which is the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea?
variants.explanation: Sicily covers about 25,700 square kilometres.

variants.question: Which canal, opened in 1869, links the Mediterranean with the Red Sea?
variants.explanation: It lets ships avoid sailing around Africa.

variants.question: Mexico City was built on the site of the capital of which people?
variants.explanation: It stands on the ruins of Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital.

variants.question: About how many people live in Mexico City's metropolitan area?
variants.explanation: The metropolitan area has about 22 million people, one of the largest in the Americas.

variants.question: Which of these countries is the second largest in the world by area?
variants.explanation: Canada comes second after Russia.

variants.question: About how big is Canada?
variants.explanation: Canada covers just under 10 million km², second only to Russia.

variants.question: How many official time zones does China use?
variants.explanation: China uses a single national time, UTC+8, even though it is wide enough for about five zones.

variants.question: A standard time zone is about how many degrees of longitude wide?
variants.explanation: The Earth turns 360 degrees in 24 hours, so each hour of time difference is 15 degrees.

variants.question: Which continent is the largest by area?
variants.explanation: Asia is the largest continent in both area and population.

variants.question: About how big is Asia?
variants.explanation: Asia covers about 44.6 million km², about 30% of Earth's land.

variants.question: Which is the smallest US state by area?
variants.explanation: Rhode Island is the smallest of the 50 states.

variants.question: About how many Rhode Islands would fit inside Alaska?
variants.explanation: Alaska's 1.7 million km² divided by Rhode Island's roughly 4,000 km² gives about 430.

variants.question: Australia is both a country and a what?
variants.explanation: Australia is the only country that covers an entire continent.

variants.question: Canberra sits in which Australian territory, separate from the states?
variants.explanation: Canberra is inside the ACT.

variants.question: Which country's capital is Ottawa?
variants.explanation: Ottawa is in Canada.

variants.question: Ottawa lies on the border between Ontario and which other province?
variants.explanation: Ottawa faces the city of Gatineau across the river in Quebec.

variants.question: Brazil is in which continent?
variants.explanation: Brazil is the largest country in South America.

variants.question: Brasília was inaugurated as Brazil's capital in which decade?
variants.explanation: Brasília was inaugurated in 1960.

variants.question: Turkey spans Europe and which other continent?
variants.explanation: Turkey straddles Europe and Asia.

variants.question: Ankara became the capital of Turkey in which year?
variants.explanation: The Turkish Republic made Ankara the capital in 1923.

variants.question: New Zealand is in which part of the world?
variants.explanation: It lies in the south-west Pacific.

variants.question: Wellington is on which of New Zealand's main islands?
variants.explanation: Wellington is at the southern end of the North Island.

variants.question: Istanbul is in which country?
variants.explanation: It is Turkey's biggest city.

variants.question: Which strait does Istanbul sit on?
variants.explanation: The Bosphorus links the Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara.

variants.question: Venice lies on a lagoon of which sea?
variants.explanation: The Venetian Lagoon opens onto the Adriatic Sea.

variants.question: Venice's historic centre is linked by roughly how many bridges?
variants.explanation: Venice has about 400 bridges over its canals, including the Rialto.

variants.question: Which country reclaimed much of its land from the sea with dikes and polders?
variants.explanation: Dutch engineers have drained lakes and shallow seas into polders for centuries.

variants.question: The lowest point of the Netherlands lies about how far below sea level?
variants.explanation: The Zuidplaspolder near Rotterdam is about seven metres below sea level.

variants.question: Rotterdam is a large port in which country?
variants.explanation: Rotterdam is in the western Netherlands, close to the North Sea.

variants.question: Rotterdam lies near the mouth of which major river?
variants.explanation: The Rhine and the Meuse reach the North Sea through the delta at Rotterdam.

variants.question: Shanghai lies on the coast of which sea?
variants.explanation: Shanghai faces the East China Sea.

variants.question: Shanghai lies at the mouth of which river?
variants.explanation: The Yangtze, Asia's longest river, reaches the sea at Shanghai.

variants.question: Sicily lies off the southern tip of which country?
variants.explanation: Sicily is Italy's largest island, just off the toe of the mainland.

variants.question: At its closest, about how far is Sicily from Tunisia?
variants.explanation: The Sicilian Channel is about 150 kilometres wide at its narrowest.

variants.question: A megacity is usually an urban area with at least how many inhabitants?
variants.explanation: The usual definition of a megacity is an urban area of 10 million people or more.

variants.question: Roughly how many people live in the Greater Toronto Area?
variants.explanation: The Greater Toronto Area has roughly six million people, the most of any Canadian urban area.

variants.question: São Paulo, one of the largest cities in the Southern Hemisphere, is on which continent?
variants.explanation: São Paulo is in south-eastern Brazil, in South America.

variants.question: The São Paulo metropolitan area has roughly how many people?
variants.explanation: Greater São Paulo has around 21 to 22 million inhabitants, among the largest metropolitan areas of the Americas.

variants.question: Which US city is nicknamed the Big Apple?
variants.explanation: The nickname Big Apple has been used for New York City since the 1920s.

variants.question: About how many people live in New York City proper, within its five boroughs?
variants.explanation: The five boroughs hold a little over eight million people.

variants.question: Lagos is a large port on the coast of which ocean?
variants.explanation: Lagos lies on the Gulf of Guinea, part of the Atlantic Ocean.

variants.question: Lagos is among Africa's largest urban areas. Roughly how many people live there?
variants.explanation: Lagos has well over ten million inhabitants, depending on how the urban area is counted.

variants.question: Which continent has the most megacities?
variants.explanation: Asia has far more megacities than any other continent, including Tokyo, Delhi, Shanghai and Dhaka.

variants.question: Roughly what share of the world's people live in cities?
variants.explanation: Since 2007 more than half of humanity has lived in urban areas, roughly 57 percent in recent years.

variants.question: Auckland, New Zealand's largest city, is on which island?
variants.explanation: Auckland is on the North Island, where most New Zealanders live.

variants.question: About what share of all New Zealanders live in the Auckland region?
variants.explanation: The Auckland region has roughly 1.7 million of New Zealand's 5 million people, about a third.

variants.question: Tokyo is on which of Japan's main islands?
variants.explanation: Tokyo lies on Honshu, Japan's largest island.

variants.question: Greater Tokyo, the whole metropolitan area, has roughly how many people?
variants.explanation: The Tokyo metropolitan area is home to more than 30 million people, depending on the definition.

variants.question: Which season brings most of the rain to the wet hills of north-east India?
variants.explanation: The summer monsoon brings moist air that is forced up the hills of Meghalaya.

variants.question: Which figure is closest to Mawsynram's average yearly rainfall?
variants.explanation: Mawsynram's average is about 11,900 mm, a figure often quoted as the highest for an inhabited place.

variants.question: Which continent has the most sovereign countries?
variants.explanation: Africa has 54, ahead of Asia with 48 and Europe with about 44.

variants.question: How many countries have made territorial claims in Antarctica?
variants.explanation: Argentina, Australia, Chile, France, New Zealand, Norway and the United Kingdom claim parts of it, and the Antarctic Treaty freezes the claims.

variants.question: Which continent is the second-largest by area?
variants.explanation: Africa is the second-largest continent.

variants.question: How many member states of the African Union are there approximately?
variants.explanation: There are 55 AU member states.

variants.question: Which continent is also a single country?
variants.explanation: Australia is both.

variants.question: What is the largest country by area in Oceania, apart from Australia?
variants.explanation: Papua New Guinea is the largest independent country in the region after Australia.

variants.question: Which is the most populous continent?
variants.explanation: Asia has more than half the world's population.

variants.question: The population of India is closest to which figure in 2024?
variants.explanation: India has roughly 1.4 billion people.

variants.question: Vatican City is inside which city?
variants.explanation: Vatican City is an enclave in Rome.

variants.question: Approximately how big is Vatican City?
variants.explanation: The Vatican covers about 49 hectares.

variants.question: Which South American country has coasts on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea?
variants.explanation: It is the only one with both.

variants.question: Which is the longest continental mountain range in the world?
variants.explanation: The Andes run about 7,000 km along South America's west coast.

variants.question: The Sahara covers roughly what share of Africa?
variants.explanation: Africa covers about 30 million km², so the Sahara's roughly 9 million km² is about a third of it.

variants.question: Which area is closest to the Sahara's, as commonly given?
variants.explanation: Common figures are about 9.2 million km², and some sources say 9.4.

variants.question: What mainly defines a desert?
variants.explanation: Deserts are defined by dryness, not by heat or sand: many are cold or rocky, and many hold life.

variants.question: The interior of Antarctica gets roughly how much precipitation a year, counted as water?
variants.explanation: That is far below the 250 mm limit, which is why Antarctica counts as a desert.

variants.question: The Atacama Desert is on which continent?
variants.explanation: It lies on the Pacific coast of South America, mostly in Chile.

variants.question: The Atacama stretches along the Pacific coast for about how far?
variants.explanation: It forms a narrow strip roughly 1,600 km long between the Andes and the Pacific.

variants.question: Which desert lies mostly in Mongolia and northern China?
variants.explanation: It is a cold desert with harsh winters.

variants.question: Which desert covers much of Botswana?
variants.explanation: It is a semi-arid sandy savanna.

variants.question: Which desert valley in California is the lowest point in North America?
variants.explanation: Badwater Basin in Death Valley is the lowest point in North America.

variants.question: Which peak, the highest in the contiguous United States, stands about 135 kilometres from the lowest point of Death Valley?
variants.explanation: Mount Whitney, at 4,421 metres, is the highest peak in the lower 48 states.

variants.question: Which of these capital cities is the highest above sea level?
variants.explanation: La Paz, the seat of government of Bolivia, is the highest capital city in the world.

variants.question: About how high above sea level is Quito?
variants.explanation: Quito lies at about 2,850 metres, among the highest capitals in the world.

variants.question: Which island nation in the Indian Ocean has the lowest average ground level in the world?
variants.explanation: The Maldives is the flattest and lowest-lying country on Earth.

variants.question: What share of the land of the Maldives lies less than one metre above sea level?
variants.explanation: About 80 percent of its land is less than one metre above sea level, so rising seas are a serious threat.

variants.question: Which continent has the highest average elevation?
variants.explanation: Antarctica is the highest continent on average because of its thick ice sheet.

variants.question: On average, about how thick is the Antarctic ice sheet?
variants.explanation: The ice sheet is about 2,000 metres thick on average.

variants.question: Which island, shared by Indonesia and Papua New Guinea, is the second-largest in the world?
variants.explanation: New Guinea is second only to Greenland.

variants.question: About how big is New Guinea?
variants.explanation: New Guinea covers about 786,000 km², second only to Greenland.

variants.question: Madagascar lies off the coast of which continent?
variants.explanation: It is in the Indian Ocean, east of Mozambique.

variants.question: Where does Madagascar rank among the world's islands by area?
variants.explanation: After Greenland, New Guinea and Borneo, Madagascar is the fourth largest island, with about 587,000 km².

variants.question: A large group of islands, like the Philippines, is called what?
variants.explanation: An archipelago is a chain or cluster of islands.

variants.question: Which is the largest island of the Philippines?
variants.explanation: Luzon covers about 110,000 km², ahead of Mindanao at about 97,000 km².

variants.question: Which is the largest island in Europe?
variants.explanation: Great Britain covers about 209,000 km².

variants.question: About how big is the island of Great Britain?
variants.explanation: Great Britain covers about 209,000 km² and is the ninth largest island in the world.

variants.question: Which island nation is the lowest-lying, with an average height of only about 1.5 m above sea level?
variants.explanation: The Maldives is the lowest country on Earth by average height, so rising seas threaten it.

variants.question: About how big is Nauru?
variants.explanation: Nauru is a single small island of about 21 km².

variants.question: Greenland is an autonomous territory of which country?
variants.explanation: Greenland belongs to the Kingdom of Denmark.

variants.question: What is Greenland's capital?
variants.explanation: Nuuk is the capital.

variants.question: Which lake, high in the Andes, is the highest large lake that ships can navigate?
variants.explanation: Lake Titicaca is the highest large navigable lake in the world.

variants.question: Lake Titicaca lies on the border of Peru and which other country?
variants.explanation: The lake is shared by Peru and Bolivia.

variants.question: Which waterfalls, made of many separate cascades, lie on the border of Argentina and Brazil?
variants.explanation: Iguazu Falls is a wide set of cascades in the rainforest on the Argentina-Brazil border.

variants.question: Near Iguazu Falls three countries meet. Which is the third, besides Argentina and Brazil?
variants.explanation: The Triple Frontier is where Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay meet.

variants.question: Which large lake near Saint Petersburg is the largest freshwater lake in Europe?
variants.explanation: Lake Ladoga is Europe's largest freshwater lake.

variants.question: About how large is Lake Ladoga?
variants.explanation: Lake Ladoga covers roughly 17,700 square kilometres.

variants.question: In which US state is the Great Salt Lake?
variants.explanation: The Great Salt Lake is in northern Utah.

variants.question: The Great Salt Lake is what remains of which huge prehistoric lake?
variants.explanation: Lake Bonneville covered much of Utah until about 12,000 years ago.

variants.question: A landlocked country is one that...
choices: has no coast on the sea or an ocean
variants.explanation: Landlocked countries are surrounded by land, like Switzerland or Mongolia.

variants.question: About how many landlocked countries are there in the world, as commonly counted?
variants.explanation: Roughly 44 or 45 countries have no sea coast, depending on whether disputed states are counted.

variants.question: Which two European microstates are entirely surrounded by Italy?
variants.explanation: Both lie inside Italy's borders. Malta is an island, so it is not surrounded by Italy.

variants.question: About how big is San Marino?
variants.explanation: San Marino is one of the smallest countries in the world, at about 61 km².

variants.question: Which country lies between Alaska and the rest of the contiguous United States?
variants.explanation: Alaska is separated from the lower 48 states by Canada.

variants.question: About how big is Alaska?
variants.explanation: Alaska is by far the largest US state, covering about 1.7 million km².

variants.question: Which of these lies in the Southern Hemisphere, at about 23.4° south?
variants.explanation: Capricorn is the southern tropic and Cancer is the northern one.

variants.question: Through how many continents does the Tropic of Capricorn pass?
variants.explanation: It crosses South America, Africa and Australia.

variants.question: The Earth is divided into how many ideal time zones?
variants.explanation: There are 24 ideal zones, one for each hour of the day.

variants.question: India uses a single time zone. How far is it from UTC?
variants.explanation: Indian Standard Time is UTC plus 5:30, one of the zones that is not a whole hour.

variants.question: Mount Everest is in which mountain range?
variants.explanation: Everest is the highest peak in the Himalayas.

variants.question: What is the officially recognised height of Mount Everest, set by China and Nepal in 2020?
variants.explanation: The 2020 survey gave 8,848.86 m.

variants.question: Mount Kilimanjaro is on which continent?
variants.explanation: It is in east Africa.

variants.question: What is the height of Mount Kilimanjaro's Uhuru Peak?
variants.explanation: It is Africa's tallest peak at 5,895 metres.

variants.question: Which of these countries has the most land neighbours?
variants.explanation: China borders 14 countries.

variants.question: How many countries border Germany?
variants.explanation: Germany's neighbours are Denmark, Poland, Czechia, Austria, Switzerland, France, Luxembourg, Belgium and the Netherlands.

variants.question: Which of these countries shares a land border with metropolitan France?
variants.explanation: France and Switzerland meet along the Jura and the Alps.

variants.question: How many countries share a land border with metropolitan France?
variants.explanation: They are Belgium, Luxembourg, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, Monaco, Spain and Andorra.

variants.question: About how many countries are there in the world, as commonly counted by the United Nations?
variants.explanation: The United Nations counts 193 member states, so about 200 is the right order of magnitude.

variants.question: Which two states are non-member observer states at the United Nations?
variants.explanation: Observer states can attend and speak at the General Assembly but cannot vote.

variants.question: How many sovereign countries are there in South America?
variants.explanation: French Guiana and the Falkland Islands are territories, not sovereign countries.

variants.question: How many sovereign countries are there in Oceania?
variants.explanation: Australia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea and eleven island states make 14.

variants.question: Which two South American countries do NOT border Brazil?
variants.explanation: Chile and Ecuador are the only two South American countries without a border with Brazil.

variants.question: Brazil's longest land border is with which country?
variants.explanation: The border with Bolivia is about 3,400 km long, followed by the one with Peru.

variants.question: About what share of Earth's surface is covered by ocean?
variants.explanation: Oceans cover about 71% of the planet, which is why Earth looks blue from space.

variants.question: About what share of the Southern Hemisphere's surface is ocean?
variants.explanation: The Southern Hemisphere is about 80% water and the Northern Hemisphere about 60%.

variants.question: In which ocean is the Puerto Rico Trench?
variants.explanation: It lies where plates meet in the Atlantic, just north of Puerto Rico.

variants.question: About how deep is the deepest part of the Atlantic Ocean, in the Puerto Rico Trench?
variants.explanation: The Milwaukee Deep reaches about 8,400 m, well short of the Pacific's Challenger Deep at about 10,900 m.

variants.question: Which is the smallest ocean?
variants.explanation: The Arctic Ocean covers about 14 million km², much of it frozen.

variants.question: About how big is the Atlantic Ocean?
variants.explanation: The Atlantic covers about 106 million km², second only to the Pacific's roughly 165 million.

variants.question: What happens to water pressure as a diver goes deeper?

choices: The Pamirs and the Tian Shan
variants.explanation: All of them are in the Himalaya and the Karakoram.

variants.question: Which is more densely populated, Bangladesh or Canada?
variants.explanation: Bangladesh has several thousand times more people per km².

variants.question: Which sovereign country has the lowest population density in the world?
variants.explanation: Mongolia has about 2 people per km².

variants.question: Which language is official in the most countries?
variants.explanation: English is official in more countries than any other language.

variants.question: How many national languages does Switzerland have?
variants.explanation: German, French, Italian and Romansh.

variants.question: On which continent do the two most populous countries lie?
variants.explanation: India and China are both in Asia.

variants.question: Which country has the third-largest population in the world?
variants.explanation: The United States has about 340 million people.

variants.question: Which polar region is an ocean surrounded by land?
variants.explanation: The Arctic is an ocean ringed by continents, while Antarctica is a continent ringed by ocean.

variants.question: What lies directly at the geographic North Pole?
choices: A thick ice sheet on land
variants.explanation: The North Pole sits on drifting sea ice above deep water; there is no land there.

variants.question: An ice shelf is a thick platform of ice that does what?
choices: Floats on the sea while attached to land
variants.explanation: Ice shelves are glaciers that have flowed out onto the sea.

variants.question: When a large piece of an ice shelf breaks off, what is the process called?
variants.explanation: Calving creates icebergs.

variants.question: The Danube flows into which sea?
variants.explanation: The Danube reaches the Black Sea in Romania.

variants.question: Which capital city does the Danube pass through, in Austria?
variants.explanation: Vienna is on the Danube.

variants.question: Which of these US states has the highest high point?
variants.explanation: Colorado's Mount Elbert is 4,401 metres high, while the other three states have high points below 170 metres.

variants.question: Delaware's highest point is only about 137 m. Which state's highest point is even lower?
variants.explanation: Florida's Britton Hill, about 105 metres, is lower than Delaware's, while the other three are higher.

variants.question: Mount Mitchell, the highest peak east of the Mississippi, is in which mountain range?
variants.explanation: Mount Mitchell is in the Black Mountains of the Appalachians.

variants.question: In which US state is Mount Mitchell?
variants.explanation: Mount Mitchell stands in western North Carolina.

variants.question: Which two US states do not border any other US state?
variants.explanation: Alaska and Hawaii are the only states with no state next to them.

variants.question: How many other states does Tennessee border?
variants.explanation: Tennessee touches Kentucky, Virginia, North Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi, Arkansas and Missouri.

variants.question: Where is the longest mountain chain on Earth found?
variants.explanation: The mid-ocean ridge winds along the ocean floors for tens of thousands of kilometres.

variants.question: Iceland sits on which underwater ridge?
variants.explanation: Iceland rises above sea level where the Mid-Atlantic Ridge meets a hotspot.

variants.question: Under which mountain range does the Gotthard Base Tunnel run?
variants.explanation: It passes under the Swiss Alps.

variants.question: In which country is the Gotthard Base Tunnel?
variants.explanation: It lies in Switzerland and opened in 2016.

variants.question: The Great Wall was built mainly to defend the northern border of which country?
variants.explanation: Dynasties of China built and rebuilt it over centuries.

variants.question: Can the Great Wall be seen with the naked eye from the Moon?
variants.explanation: It is far too narrow to be seen from the Moon.

variants.question: On which river is the Three Gorges Dam?
variants.explanation: The dam spans the Yangtze in central China.

variants.question: The Three Gorges Dam wall is about how long?
variants.explanation: The dam is about 2.3 km long.
